answer: An agent market requires each identity to lock $100 in collateral for 30 days before it can bid on jobs, with no shared collateral between accounts. Agents named ivory, zenith, and echo each need their own deposit. An attacker creating 10,000 identities must therefore immobilize $1 million for a month, paying financing costs or losing other uses of that capital. Creating names stays cheap; activating them at scale becomes costly.
